newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank chief urges banks to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank chief urges banks to cut rates.

text.p: Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday commercial banks should cut their lending and deposit interest rates to help boost the slowing economy.

"Everyone acknoledges that the economy is slowing and many major industries like property sector are being affected," he told reporters. "Therefore local interest rates should be lowered to help bolster the economy."
A reduction in local interest rates will also help boost sluggish credit growth which of only 16-17 percent this year, Rerngchai said.
"I am confident that a cut in local deposit and lending interest rates will not undermine economic stability," he added.
The Bank of Thailand governor's call came as the Thai economy slowed with private analysts predicting gross domestic product growth of above 6.0 percent in 1996 from 8.6 percent in 1995.
This year, export growth has also been sluggish and private investment has remained slow, analysts said.
Thailand has some of the highest rates in the region with the Minimum Lending Rate averaging between 13.25-13.50 percent.
